transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What has brought you in to see me today?

Yeah… I guess what brought me in is I’m losing a lot of time rechecking things. Like, my dressing supplies, door locks, file dimensions, revision notes—stuff like that. I’ll try to move on, but it feels like I’m not really allowed to until I’ve gone through the same routine enough times that the anxiety drops.

And it sounds silly when I say it out loud, because I’m an engineer, so checking details is kind of part of the job, you know? Like dimensions and revisions matter. But this is different. It’s not just being careful—it turns into hours sometimes, and then I’m late or I can’t focus on the next thing because my mind is still stuck on whether I checked it “right.”

When you feel the need to recheck things, is it because you get specific, intrusive thoughts or images that something bad will happen if you don’t do it a certain way, even though you know they don’t really make sense?

Yeah, that’s pretty much it. It’s like even after I know I cleaned the wound area, or I know I reviewed the CAD file, this thought cuts back in—like, what if I missed one tiny thing? And then it jumps to, you know, the wound gets infected, or there’s some design mistake that could hurt someone.

And I can tell myself, “No, I already checked that,” but it doesn’t really stick. I mean, at work, missing a detail can matter, so it’s not totally out of nowhere, I guess… but this feels different. Like my brain won’t accept the answer, even when I know I’ve done it.
Because of this rechecking and the anxiety around it, how much is it actually interfering with your day-to-day life—for example, making you late, hurting your work, or affecting your relationships?

It’s… yeah, it’s starting to mess things up more than I wanted to admit. At work especially, my project deadlines have started slipping because I’ll stay late trying to get comfortable enough to actually submit something. Like I’ll be there after everyone’s gone, still checking a file or notes, and then I tell myself it’s just being thorough—but it’s not really efficient anymore.

And outside work, I’ve stopped making it to paddleboarding meetups, which is annoying because that used to be kind of my reset. Same with workouts. I’ll think, “I’ll just do the routine and then go,” but then the checking eats up the time I had set aside, and by the time I’m done it’s too late or I’m too drained. So… yeah, it’s not ruining everything, but it’s definitely getting in the way.
When you get stuck rechecking, in that moment do you feel like the level of checking you’re doing is clearly excessive or unreasonable, or does it mostly feel justified to you?

In the moment, it kind of feels justified… like I know that sounds weird, but if I’m checking dressing supplies or a door lock or file dimensions, my brain is saying, “No, this is important, you can’t move on yet.”

Then later I can see it’s excessive, because I’ve lost hours to it. Like I’ll have gone through the same routine again and again just waiting for the anxiety to drop enough. It’s almost like I’m not allowed to stop until it feels right, even if part of me knows I already checked.

Outside of these specific situations where you’re rechecking things, do you also find yourself worrying a lot about many different everyday things—like money, health, work performance, or family—most days, even when nothing in particular has gone wrong?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I worry about work, but it usually hooks onto a specific thing I’m checking, if that makes sense. Like a drawing or a measurement or whether I did something right.

Money or family stuff… I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about all of that most days. Or, well, sometimes I’ll think about money because rent is ridiculous, and then I start thinking about how my friend somehow found a cheaper place across town, but that’s not really the same thing, I guess.

So… I don’t think it’s a broad, everything-all-the-time kind of worry. It’s more tied to those specific situations.

Apart from physically rechecking things, do you also find yourself doing mental rituals—like repeatedly going over events, numbers, or phrases in your head in a very specific way—to try to feel less anxious or prevent something bad from happening?

Um… not really in the sense of, like, repeating a phrase in my head or doing numbers a certain way. It’s more physical, I guess, or routine-based.

Like what brings me in is that I’m losing hours to rechecking actual things—my dressing supplies, door locks, file dimensions, revision notes—because I don’t feel allowed to move on until I’ve gone through the same routine enough times that the anxiety finally drops. And sometimes I’ll be thinking through, like, “Did I check that? Did I miss that?” but it’s usually tied to the checking itself, not some separate mental ritual.

Sorry, I’m probably overexplaining. It’s just… it’s the repeating and rechecking that gets me stuck.
How long have you been having these rechecking routines and feeling like you can’t move on until they feel “right”?

It’s been long enough that it’s not just a bad week or something. I guess I noticed it most because I started losing actual hours to it—like with dressing supplies, or checking the door lock, or going back through file dimensions and revision notes at work.

And it’s weird because I’ll think, okay, I checked it, but then I still can’t move on until I’ve gone through the routine again and again and the anxiety drops. Sorry, that doesn’t exactly answer how long. I’m not great at pinning down the start. It kind of built up gradually, I think.
Thinking back, would you say these rechecking routines have been going on for at least a year, or has it been less than a year so far?

I think… yeah, it’s been going on a while. I don’t know if I can put an exact date on it, but it’s definitely not just the last couple months.

What made me finally pay attention is that I’m losing hours to it now—like rechecking my dressing supplies, the door locks, file dimensions, revision notes at work. I’ll tell myself I already checked, but I still don’t feel like I can move on until I’ve gone through the routine enough times and the anxiety comes down.

So, I guess… at least long enough that it’s become a real pattern. I’m sorry, I know you asked year or less than a year—I’m leaning toward at least a year, but I’m not great at marking when it started.

When you try to resist or cut short the checking routines—for example, deciding you will check something only once and then stop—does your anxiety or discomfort quickly build up to the point that it feels almost impossible not to go back and check again?

Yeah… that’s pretty much what happens. I’ll decide, like, okay, I’m only going to check the door once, or I already looked at the dressing supplies, and then I’ll try to walk away—but it doesn’t feel finished.

It’s like this pressure builds, like I’m not allowed to move on yet. And then I start thinking about whether I missed something, and I end up going back into the same routine. Same with work stuff too, like file dimensions or revision notes—I know that sounds boring, but I can lose so much time because I keep needing to recheck until the anxiety comes down.

Sorry, I started thinking about work there. But yeah, if I cut it short, it gets really uncomfortable fast, and checking again feels like the only way to make it settle.

Outside of the moments when you’re actively checking things, do you ever get sudden, unwanted thoughts or images about something terrible happening that pop into your mind and feel intrusive, like they don’t fit with what you actually want or believe?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not just when I’m standing there checking. Like even after I know I cleaned the wound area, or I’ve already reviewed a CAD file, this thought just cuts in like, what if you missed one tiny thing?

And then it sort of runs with it—like the wound could get infected, or the design mistake could hurt someone. I know that sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, because at work there are reviews and standards and, you know, it’s not like one dimension should become this whole disaster in my head. But the thought doesn’t really care about that.

It feels intrusive, yeah. Like I don’t want it there, and I can’t just reason it away by telling myself I already checked.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has recurrent, intrusive doubts about having made dangerous mistakes (e.g., wound care, engineering files) that are experienced as unwanted and excessive, and engages in repetitive checking rituals (locks, dressing supplies, file dimensions, revision notes) until anxiety decreases. Attempts to resist these rituals lead to rapidly escalating anxiety and a strong sense of not being able to move on until the routine feels 'right.' These symptoms have been present for at least many months (likely ≥1 year), consume hours of time, and cause clear functional impairment at work and in leisure activities. Worry is not generalized across multiple life domains, arguing against generalized anxiety disorder. There is no clear primary depressive syndrome or simple stress-related overwork pattern. This presentation is most consistent with obsessive–compulsive disorder (F42).
